Performers
Johanna Gadski (soprano), Frank La Forge (piano) Documented

The label reads ‘Soprano with pianoforte’ and names Johanna Gadski; the Discography of American Historical Recordings names La Forge as pianist.

[2] [3]
Work version
Beach’s Browning setting, recorded as the second song on a single-faced 10-inch side, after Frank La Forge’s “How Much I Love You” Documented

The label lists both songs, (a) La Forge and (b) Beach. The key sung and any cuts or changes to the printed song are not established.

[2] [3] [5]
Recorded
1908-01-14 Documented

Matrix B-5018, take 2; the date is also handwritten on the label.

[3] [2]
Place
New York, New York, United States Documented

Recording place from the Discography of American Historical Recordings; no studio address is given.

[3]
Label
Victor Talking Machine Company, Red Seal Documented

Single-faced 10-inch disc.

[2] [4]
Catalogue
Victor 87026 Documented

Listed on the Gadski page of the Victor catalogue of July 1909.

[2] [4] [5]
Matrix, take, sides
B-5018, take 2 Documented

Take 1 was held; take 2 was the master issued as 87026.

[3] [1]
Transfer
Library of Congress Packard Campus for Audio Visual Conservation; National Jukebox MP3 mirrored by Hessel Digital Library Documented

Credits as stated in the Internet Archive item, which links to the National Jukebox record and notes Sony Music Entertainment or EMI Music as the source of the disc.

[1]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

The digitisation date is not given. The mirror was added to the Internet Archive on 18 October 2026, a copying event.

[1]
Processing
Unknown Unknown

Playback speed, stylus, equalisation and noise reduction are not stated. A separate Great 78 Project transfer of the same disc is about seven per cent longer, so the speed of the Library’s copy is not certain.

[1]
Composition rights
Out of copyright: Beach died in 1944, Browning in 1889 and La Forge in 1953. Inferred, not documented

Life-plus-70 terms have run out for all three; the 1900 edition was published in the United States. This covers the historical songs, not modern editions.

[3]
Recording rights
US public domain: first published 1908 or 1909 on Victor 87026; the mirror carries the Public Domain Mark. Documented

Selected under the project’s us-published-before-cutoff rule. The July 1909 Victor catalogue lists the disc; the Library of Congress gives 1908. The Public Domain Mark is a status declaration, not a new licence.

[1] [5] [3]

Amy Beach, The Year’s at the Spring, Op. 44 No. 1, with Frank La Forge’s How Much I Love You. Johanna Gadski, soprano; Frank La Forge, piano. Victor 87026 (matrix B-5018-2, 14 January 1908). Library of Congress National Jukebox transfer, mirrored by Hessel Digital Library on Internet Archive. Rights statement
